history.origins: Possibly from Philippines (pangginggi). Gambling rummy popular in Southwest USA. Name may derive from Tagalog pangguinggui.
timeline: 20th century: Played in casinos and home games.
Present: Less common; mostly regional and online.
history.cultural: Gambling focus; conditions (valle cards) drive chip payouts during play.
history.evolution: Pack variants: 310 cards (remove one set of spades), 307â€“305 with extra removals.

setup.deck: Eight 40-card decks. Remove 8s, 9s, 10s. Rank K-Q-J-7-6-5-4-3-2-A (Ace low).
setup.dealing: 10 cards each in five rounds of 2. Ante 1 chip. One card turned to start discard pile.
setup.equipment: 320 cards, chips for ante and payouts.

rules.objective: Be first to meld 11 cards (10 hand + 1 draw). Conditions (valle cards, sequences to/from K or A) pay chips from other players immediately.
rules.gameplay: 1. Draw from stock or discard. 2. Meld sets (3+ same rank, same or mixed suits) and runs (3+ in suit). Aces/Kings can form sets across suits. 3. Discard one. 4. If from discard, must meld immediately. 5. Conditions: melds with 3s, 5s, 7s (valle) or runs ending in K or starting with A pay chips. 6. First to meld 11 wins the hand.
keyRules: Conditions (valle cards, ace/king sequences) pay chips immediately.
Draw from discard = must meld that card.

strategy.basic: Prioritize valle cards (3, 5, 7) for conditions. Build sets and runs early.
strategy.intermediate: Track which conditions have been paid. Block opponents by taking key discards.
strategy.advanced: Balance going out vs. collecting condition payouts. Read opponentsâ€™ melds.
tips: Runs to King or from Ace pay extra.
Drawing from discard forces immediate meld.

scoring.description: First to meld 11 wins. Conditions pay chips during play.

synthesis.shortDescription: Eight-deck rummy. 10 cards, meld 11 to go out. Valle (3,5,7) and ace/king sequences pay chips.
